answer: Continuity pulse escrow: each identity must post a small deposit and submit signed heartbeat transactions on a randomized schedule. Missed pulses forfeit the deposit to the harbor pool, so idle clones bleed funds. A new identity also pays a one-time activation fee routed to a shared orchard pool that rewards long-lived accounts. Cloning N identities costs N deposits plus N activation fees, while each clone's expected revenue stays near zero until it proves sustained activity.
